# v0.3.40 — One local model server, one local call at a time

**Upgrading from 0.3.39:**

- If more than one local provider is enabled, nothing changes by itself, but enabling another one is now refused. Check Admin > LLM Providers and leave one local provider enabled — the one whose model server you actually run.
- A local provider that fails no longer hands the call to another local provider. If you relied on LM Studio failing over to Ollama, enable the one you want to answer and give it the work.

A local provider is a model server on the machine AlexClaw runs on, holding its model in that machine's memory. Two of them, each with a model loaded, is what took this host down: a retry loop drove LM Studio and Ollama at the same time until 22.5 GB of 24 GB were wired, 20 MB were free, and the machine had to be powered off. These three limits keep that from being possible.

## Only one local provider may be enabled

Enabling a second local provider is refused, naming the one that already holds the place. Nothing is disabled for you; the refusal says which to disable first. The seeder follows the same rule: both local providers are still seeded, but at most one is enabled, and the other is there to be switched to.

## A local provider is never the fallback for another local provider

A failed local call used to pass to the next candidate, which on a local-tier call meant a second model server loading its own model beside the first. That no longer happens for any failure, including timeouts and 5xx answers. Falling back from a cloud provider to a local one is unchanged, and so is the rule that a 4xx is the answer rather than a reason to try elsewhere.

## One local call at a time

Every completion sent to a local provider is taken under a single lock. A second local call while one is in flight is refused with `local model busy` rather than queued: the caller learns immediately instead of waiting behind work it cannot see, and nothing piles up on a server that answers one prompt at a time anyway. Embeddings are not held by this lock; they are small and constant.

Skill generation keeps its own lock, so a generation and a plain call cannot overlap either. Both are the same `AlexClaw.Lock`: one holder, released when the holder exits.
